items.description: Analyze repository structure and document all modules, agents, and tooling
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/concept_evolve/repo_analysis.json containing: (a) every module in .archivara/ (concept_evolve.py, semantic_scholar.py, opencode.json) with its purpose and public API, (b) every tool in .opencode/tools/ (concept_evolve.ts, semantic_scholar.ts) with invocation signatures, (c) every agent in .opencode/agents/ (concept-tree-explorer.md, literature-graph-miner.md) with capabilities and tool access, (d) agent roles from opencode.json (orchestrator, researcher, writer, reviewer, concept_worker), (e) inter-module dependency graph. File must be valid JSON with at least 8 module/tool/agent entries.

items.description: Conduct comprehensive web search for parallel DEFLATE decompression literature
items.acceptance_criteria: Use websearch and webfetch to find at least 20 relevant sources on: (a) parallel decompression of DEFLATE/LZ77/Huffman streams, (b) speculative parallel parsing of compressed data (e.g., pugz by Lecompte et al.), (c) GPU-accelerated decompression (nvcomp, GDeflate), (d) SIMD-optimized decompression (libdeflate, ISA-L, zlib-ng), (e) file-level parallelism in ZIP archives (pigz, parallel-unzip), (f) alternative entropy coding amenable to parallelism. Save raw search results with URLs, titles, and relevance notes to results/concept_evolve/literature_search_raw.json. Must cover at least 4 of the 6 listed sub-topics.
items.notes: Requires websearch tool. This is the foundation for all subsequent literature items.

items.description: Build citation graph using Semantic Scholar seeded by core parallel decompression papers
items.acceptance_criteria: Use the semantic_scholar tool (graph command) with at least 3 seed queries: 'parallel DEFLATE decompression', 'speculative parallel LZ77 decoding', 'GPU lossless decompression'. Merge results into a single graph saved to results/concept_evolve/citation_graph.json with at least 25 unique nodes and 15 edges. Identify the top-5 most-cited hub papers by citation count. Requires subagent delegation: use literature-graph-miner to traverse citation chains and identify cross-domain transfer opportunities.
items.notes: Subagent delegation: literature-graph-miner for citation chain traversal and cross-domain transfer identification.

items.description: Create and populate sources.bib with BibTeX entries for all consulted sources
items.acceptance_criteria: Create sources.bib in the repo root containing valid BibTeX entries for at least 10 relevant papers/sources. Must include entries for: (1) libdeflate by Eric Biggers, (2) zlib-ng project, (3) Intel ISA-L, (4) pugz by Lecompte et al. 2019/2021, (5) GDeflate/nvcomp by NVIDIA, (6) at least one paper on speculative decompression or speculative parallel parsing, (7) at least one paper on SIMD Huffman decoding, (8) RFC 1951 (DEFLATE spec), (9) at least one paper on work-stealing schedulers, (10) at least one paper on memory-bandwidth-bound algorithms. Each entry must have title, author/organization, year, and URL or DOI fields.
items.notes: Use semantic_scholar bibtex command where paper IDs are available; manually compose entries for tools/RFCs.

items.description: Run ConceptEvolve to generate cross-domain concept tree for parallel decompression
items.acceptance_criteria: Execute concept_evolve evolve with topic 'Fast parallel decompression of DEFLATE streams in ZIP archives targeting 3x throughput over libdeflate on multi-core x86-64'. Verify results/concept_evolve/tree/ contains at least 8 concept folders each with concept.json and README.md. Verify results/concept_evolve/concept_cards.json (array of >=8 cards), semantic_bridge.json (with nodes and edges arrays), introspection.json (with blind_spots key), and steering_directions.json (array of >=3 items) all exist and are valid JSON. Use concept-tree-explorer subagent to traverse and score the generated paths.
items.notes: Subagent delegation: concept-tree-explorer for path traversal and scoring after evolve completes.

items.description: Synthesize problem decomposition from literature review and concept tree
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/concept_evolve/problem_decomposition.md that decomposes the DEFLATE parallel decompression challenge into at least 5 independent sub-problems: (1) DEFLATE block boundary detection in a compressed bitstream, (2) Huffman table reconstruction at arbitrary entry points without prior context, (3) LZ77 back-reference resolution across speculative segment boundaries, (4) work partitioning and dynamic load balancing across heterogeneous segments, (5) correctness verification and cross-boundary fixup. Each sub-problem must: reference at least 2 entries from sources.bib, link to at least 1 relevant concept folder in results/concept_evolve/tree/, and state the key technical obstacle preventing trivial parallelization.

items.description: Build and benchmark libdeflate as the single-threaded reference baseline
items.acceptance_criteria: Clone and build libdeflate from source (latest release). Create a benchmark harness that decompresses at least 3 real-world ZIP files (each >=100 MB): (a) one with many small files (>1000 members), (b) one with few large files (<10 members), (c) one mixed-size archive. Record per-file and aggregate: throughput in MB/s, wall-clock time in ms, peak RSS in MB. Run each test case at least 5 times and report mean and standard deviation. Save results to results/baselines/libdeflate_benchmark.json with all raw data points.

items.description: Benchmark additional baselines: zlib-ng, ISA-L, pigz, and system unzip
items.acceptance_criteria: Build and benchmark zlib-ng (latest), Intel ISA-L (latest), pigz, and system unzip on the same 3-file test corpus from item_007. Save results to results/baselines/all_baselines.json. For each tool record: throughput (MB/s), wall-clock time (ms), peak RSS (MB), and number of threads used. Document which axis of parallelism each tool exploits (pigz: per-file only; ISA-L: SIMD within stream; zlib-ng: SIMD Huffman). Include a comparison table showing relative throughput vs. libdeflate. Requires subagent delegation: use explore subagent to identify build flags and optimal configurations for each tool.
items.notes: Subagent delegation: general agent to research optimal build configurations for each baseline tool.

items.description: Profile DEFLATE decompression to quantify bottleneck distribution
items.acceptance_criteria: Use perf stat and perf record (or equivalent Linux profiling) on libdeflate decompression of the largest test file. Produce results/baselines/profile_report.json documenting: (a) time breakdown: Huffman decoding vs. LZ77 copy/match vs. I/O (percentages summing to 100%), (b) IPC (instructions per cycle), (c) L1/L2/L3 cache miss rates, (d) branch misprediction rate, (e) measured memory bandwidth utilization as percentage of theoretical maximum (from lscpu or stream benchmark). This data determines whether the bottleneck is compute-bound, memory-bound, or latency-bound.

items.description: Characterize DEFLATE stream structure of the test corpus
items.acceptance_criteria: Write an analysis tool (Python or C) to parse DEFLATE streams from the test corpus and produce results/baselines/stream_analysis.json containing: (a) total block count per file, (b) block type distribution (stored/static Huffman/dynamic Huffman as percentages), (c) average and median compressed block size in bytes, (d) LZ77 back-reference distance distribution (percentage within 256B, 1KB, 4KB, 16KB, 32KB), (e) average match length, (f) ratio of literal bytes to back-reference bytes. This directly determines which intra-stream parallelism strategies are feasible based on back-reference reach.

items.description: Define target metrics, success criteria, and hardware specification
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/baselines/target_metrics.md specifying: (a) primary success metric: aggregate decompression throughput in GB/s over the full test corpus, (b) target: >=3x the libdeflate throughput measured in item_007, (c) secondary metrics: parallel efficiency (speedup/threads), memory overhead ratio (peak RSS parallel / peak RSS sequential), latency to first decompressed byte, (d) full hardware specification: CPU model and microarchitecture, core/thread count, L1/L2/L3 cache sizes, DRAM bandwidth (from stream benchmark), OS and kernel version. Reference the measured baseline numbers.

items.description: Design and prototype speculative multi-entry-point intra-stream parallel decompression
items.acceptance_criteria: Implement a prototype (C/C++ or Rust) that: (1) divides a single DEFLATE stream into N segments at evenly-spaced byte offsets, (2) at each split point scans forward to sync onto a valid Huffman block boundary using heuristic validation (check BTYPE bits, attempt trial Huffman table parse), (3) speculatively decompresses each segment in parallel with independent output buffers, (4) resolves cross-boundary LZ77 back-references in a sequential merge pass copying from prior segments' output. Measure on at least 2 test files: sync success rate (target: >80% within 1KB scan), wasted-work percentage, and raw throughput at 4 threads. Document the algorithm with pseudocode in a concept folder at results/concept_evolve/tree/ with concept.json and README.md. Must cite pugz (from sources.bib) and explicitly document differences in approach.
items.notes: Core novel contribution #1. Builds on item_010 stream analysis to choose split heuristics.

items.description: Design and prototype ZIP-level file-parallel decompression with work-stealing
items.acceptance_criteria: Implement a multi-threaded ZIP decompressor (C/C++ or Rust) that: (1) parses the ZIP central directory to enumerate all member files and their compressed sizes, (2) dispatches per-file DEFLATE decompression tasks to a work-stealing thread pool, (3) uses mmap or pread for concurrent I/O to avoid contention, (4) handles stored (uncompressed) members as zero-cost tasks. Measure throughput on all 3 test corpus types at 1/4/8/16 threads. Save prototype to results/prototypes/zip_parallel/ and design document to a concept folder in results/concept_evolve/tree/.

items.description: Design hybrid two-level parallelism combining file-level and intra-stream approaches
items.acceptance_criteria: Design and implement a scheduling system that: outer level assigns ZIP members to threads (from item_013), inner level applies speculative intra-stream parallelism (from item_012) to individual members exceeding a configurable size threshold (e.g., >1 MB compressed). Document the scheduling policy including: thread pool sizing heuristic, threshold selection rationale, expected speedup model using Amdahl's law with serial fractions measured in item_009. Produce results/concept_evolve/tree/NNN_hybrid_parallel/concept.json with the mathematical speedup model and results/prototypes/hybrid_parallel/ with prototype code.

items.description: Prototype SIMD-accelerated block boundary detection and Huffman table validation
items.acceptance_criteria: Implement a SIMD scanner (SSE4.2 or AVX2) that rapidly identifies candidate DEFLATE block boundaries by: (a) scanning for BFINAL+BTYPE bit patterns at byte-aligned and sub-byte offsets, (b) performing lightweight Huffman table header validation at each candidate. Measure: scanning throughput in GB/s (target: >10 GB/s), false positive rate (target: <10%), and end-to-end improvement when integrated into the speculative decompressor from item_012. Save to results/prototypes/simd_scanner/.

items.description: Investigate cache-aware output buffer management and prefetch optimization
items.acceptance_criteria: Prototype explicit software prefetch instructions (prefetchnta/prefetcht0) and cache-line-aligned output buffer partitioning for the parallel decompressor. Measure cache miss rates and compare against naive allocation (from item_009 baseline). Document L1/L2/L3 utilization patterns. Target: >=20% reduction in L2 cache misses vs. naive parallel allocation. Save measurements and analysis to results/prototypes/cache_optimization/.

items.description: Concept-tree expansion: probe blind spots and explore alternative paradigms
items.acceptance_criteria: Use ConceptEvolve probe on at least 2 blind spots identified in results/concept_evolve/introspection.json. Run ConceptEvolve reframe on the core problem statement. Verify results/concept_evolve/probe_result.json contains at least 3 steering_directions and results/concept_evolve/reframings.json contains at least 6 domain reframings. Integrate at least 1 novel direction (not already covered by items 012-016) into a new concept folder under results/concept_evolve/tree/ with concept.json and README.md. Requires subagent delegation: concept-tree-explorer to identify the highest-value unexplored paths and literature-graph-miner to find supporting evidence for new directions.
items.notes: Subagent delegation: concept-tree-explorer + literature-graph-miner for exploration and evidence gathering.

items.description: Assemble comprehensive benchmark suite with diverse real-world ZIP files
items.acceptance_criteria: Collect at least 6 ZIP files (each >=100 MB) covering diverse workloads: (a) Linux kernel source tarball (.tar.gz repackaged as .zip), (b) game asset archive (textures/models), (c) Java application (.jar or .war), (d) document collection (.docx or .epub files zipped), (e) scientific dataset (CSV/HDF5 zipped), (f) software distribution package. For each file document: total compressed size, total uncompressed size, compression ratio, member count, min/max/median member size. Save manifest to results/experiments/benchmark_suite.json.

items.description: Run thread-scaling experiments: throughput vs. thread count for all approaches
items.acceptance_criteria: For each prototype (file-parallel from item_013, speculative intra-stream from item_012, hybrid from item_014) and all baselines, measure decompression throughput at thread counts {1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 16} on all benchmark files. Run 5 repetitions per configuration. Save raw data to results/experiments/scaling_data.json. Generate scaling plots saved to figures/scaling_file_parallel.png, figures/scaling_speculative.png, figures/scaling_hybrid.png. Identify which approach first exceeds 3x libdeflate throughput and at what thread count. Compute parallel efficiency (speedup / thread_count) for each configuration.

items.description: Measure speculative decompression accuracy and overhead at varying split granularity
items.acceptance_criteria: For the speculative parallel approach (item_012), measure at split counts {2, 4, 8, 16, 32}: (a) block boundary sync success rate, (b) wasted work as percentage of total decompressed bytes, (c) merge-pass wall-clock overhead as percentage of total time, (d) byte-for-byte correctness vs. libdeflate reference output (must be 100%). Test on all benchmark files. Save to results/experiments/speculation_accuracy.json. Target: >=90% sync success rate with <=15% wasted work at 8 splits.

items.description: Compare achieved throughput against published numbers from prior work in the literature
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/experiments/literature_comparison.json comparing the best achieved throughput of each prototype against published numbers from: pugz, ISA-L, zlib-ng, libdeflate, GDeflate/nvcomp, and any other tools found in the Phase 1 literature search. Normalize comparisons to account for hardware differences (report as percentage of memory bandwidth, or throughput per core at comparable clock speed). Reference specific BibTeX keys from sources.bib for each comparison. Include at least 6 prior-work data points. Requires subagent delegation: literature-graph-miner to extract and cross-verify published throughput numbers from papers.
items.notes: Subagent delegation: literature-graph-miner to extract and verify published performance numbers.

items.description: Ablation study: isolate contribution of each parallelism and optimization component
items.acceptance_criteria: Measure throughput with each component toggled independently on the full benchmark suite: (a) file-level parallelism only, (b) intra-stream speculation only, (c) SIMD block boundary detection on/off, (d) prefetch and cache optimization on/off, (e) work-stealing scheduler vs. static partitioning, (f) full hybrid. Present results as a table in results/experiments/ablation.json showing marginal throughput contribution (GB/s delta) and percentage improvement of each component. Identify the single most impactful component.

items.description: Verify decompression correctness across edge cases and adversarial inputs
items.acceptance_criteria: Verify byte-identical output against libdeflate reference for: (a) all 6 benchmark files, (b) ZIP files with stored (uncompressed) members mixed with DEFLATE members, (c) ZIP files using ZIP64 extensions (>4 GB), (d) DEFLATE streams with maximum back-reference distance (32768 bytes) across every block boundary, (e) single-block DEFLATE streams, (f) empty members (0-byte files). Report 100% pass rate. Save detailed pass/fail report to results/experiments/correctness_report.json with SHA-256 checksums for both reference and test outputs.

items.description: Write final results analysis with statistical rigor and comparison to prior work
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/analysis/final_results.md containing: (a) summary table of all approaches vs. all baselines with mean throughput, standard deviation, and 95% confidence intervals, (b) best achieved speedup over libdeflate with paired t-test or Wilcoxon signed-rank test (p < 0.05), (c) analysis of which workload characteristics (file count, member size distribution, compression ratio, back-reference distance distribution) predict where each approach excels or fails, (d) Amdahl's law analysis comparing theoretical maximum speedup (from item_009 serial fraction) to measured speedup and explaining any gap, (e) comparison to at least 5 entries from sources.bib with normalized throughput.

items.description: Generate publication-quality figures for all key results
items.acceptance_criteria: Generate and save to figures/: (a) throughput_comparison.png — grouped bar chart of all approaches on all benchmarks with error bars, (b) scaling_efficiency.png — parallel efficiency (speedup/threads) vs. thread count for all approaches, (c) speculation_tradeoff.png — sync success rate and wasted work vs. number of split points, (d) ablation_waterfall.png — waterfall chart showing cumulative throughput contribution of each component, (e) architecture_diagram.png — system architecture of the hybrid approach showing data flow. All figures: labeled axes, legends, >=300 DPI, colorblind-friendly palette.

items.description: Document limitations, failure modes, and future research directions
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/analysis/limitations.md covering: (a) workloads where the approach does NOT achieve 3x speedup (with quantitative data from experiments), (b) failure modes of speculative decompression including adversarial inputs and pathological block structures, (c) memory overhead scaling with thread count, (d) applicability to gzip-only streams (no ZIP central directory) and .gz/.png/.jar formats, (e) comparison to GPU approaches (GDeflate) including when GPU offload would win, (f) at least 4 concrete future research directions with rationale. Must cite at least 3 entries from sources.bib.

items.description: Compile concept-tree final state, walk productive paths, and write research narrative
items.acceptance_criteria: Use ConceptEvolve walk to traverse the final concept tree. Produce results/concept_evolve/final_narrative.md that: (a) lists all concept folders in results/concept_evolve/tree/ with their final status, (b) traces the 3 most productive concept paths and explains what each contributed to the final design, (c) identifies which cross-domain bridges from semantic_bridge.json yielded actionable algorithmic insights, (d) documents which steering directions from Phase 1 were pursued, which were abandoned, and why, (e) lists at least 2 concepts that were explored but proved unviable, with the specific evidence that led to their abandonment. Requires subagent delegation: concept-tree-explorer to score all paths and identify the most productive trajectories.
items.notes: Subagent delegation: concept-tree-explorer for comprehensive path scoring and narrative synthesis.

items.description: Produce reproducibility package with build instructions, scripts, and final sources.bib validation
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/analysis/reproducibility.md with: (a) exact build instructions for all prototypes including compiler version, flags, and dependencies, (b) test corpus acquisition or generation scripts (download URLs or generation commands), (c) command-line invocations to reproduce every benchmark result in results/experiments/, (d) hardware and software specifications (CPU, RAM, OS, kernel, compiler versions), (e) expected approximate runtimes for each experiment. Validate sources.bib: must contain >=10 entries, every entry must be referenced at least once across all .md files in results/. Validate all .json files in results/ are syntactically valid JSON.
